title: The Blaschka Object Network — Consular Certification and Route Documentation Register
scope: Primary-source evidence showing U.S. consular certification and consular-post infrastructure as part of Blaschka transatlantic shipment practice, plus the federal archival record group in which post-level documentation may survive.
methodological_guard: The existence of U.S. consular records for Germany does not prove that a Blaschka consular certificate or invoice is preserved in Record Group 84. Workshop-side certificates and correspondence are direct evidence; RG 84 is the government-side retrieval universe. Bremen is named in the Blaschka correspondence, but a surviving Bremen-post file must be located through NARA finding aids before a specific archival citation is asserted.

events.event: Insured Harvard shipment with consular invoice
events.evidence: Rudolf's dispatch letter says the Bremen-bound Harvard consignment was insured and that a consular invoice had been made out to the value of approximately three years of work.
events.research_value: The shipment acquired an official declared-value identity before ocean carriage, distinct from the workshop's internal model prices and later freight/customs charges.

events.event: Return of the American consulate in Bremen as a condition for resumed trade
events.evidence: While planning the first major postwar shipment, Rudolf wrote that one sign of progress was that 'we have now the American consulate again in Bremen', but that a renewed commercial treaty was still needed to restore the old order. He simultaneously described export declaration, licensing and taxation as unresolved obstacles.
events.research_value: Consular presence itself appears as part of the infrastructure that made a familiar shipping route usable again after war and regulatory rupture.

events.event: Cheaper direct-Boston route rejected because it would require new consular paperwork
events.evidence: Ehrhorn, Emden & Mayer proposed direct Bremen-to-Boston carriage, but Rudolf rejected the cheaper route because changing the already prepared itinerary would require a new consular certificate/invoice and create delay. He retained the New York-in-bond-to-Boston route.
events.research_value: Documentation created path dependence: once consular paperwork was prepared for one route, the cheaper physical route could become administratively more expensive.

events.event: Consular Certificate for Shipment to Harvard University
events.evidence: The Rakow finding aid explicitly lists a 1932 'Consular Certificate for Shipment to Harvard University' in Series 04, Business Files.
events.research_value: A surviving formal consular document can be read against the 1932 invoice, crate sketches, shipment contents and Harvard arrival/unpacking correspondence.

government_archive_target.reference: Record Group 84 — Records of Foreign Service Posts of the Department of State
relevant_record_types: records relating to U.S. vessels and cargo
certifications of merchandise shipped from or received in the consular district
records of notarial, shipping and other fees
government_archive_target.recordkeeping_note: For 1912–1948, post files are generally grouped by year/block of years and arranged by a subject decimal filing scheme. Additional finding aids, including Special List 9, are required to identify exact Bremen/Dresden post holdings.
research_questions: Do Bremen consular files preserve certificates, invoices, fee records or local correspondence for Blaschka/Harvard consignments in 1906, 1923, 1929 or 1932?
Can consular certification dates be matched to Ehrhorn, Emden & Mayer forwarding dates and Norddeutscher Lloyd sailings?
Do local business correspondence files document route changes, export certification or the re-establishment of American consular services after World War I?

research_observation: Consular paperwork was not a passive certificate added after a route had been chosen. It helped constitute the route. The 1929 refusal to adopt a cheaper direct-Boston service because new consular documentation would be required makes administrative paperwork an observable source of logistical path dependence.
